text.p: Shares of Indonesian cigarette maker PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna tumbled 8.40 percent to 19,350 rupiah in early trade on Tuesday.
Brokers said major sell orders from foreign houses sent shares in the tobacco company plunging.
"Almost all big foreign houses were seen unloading the shares. I think it was linked to its investment in Astra International," one major foreign broker said.
Astra is the country's largest automobile maker.

Sampoerna topped the net losers' list on Tuesday, with about 235,000 shares changing hands. The share fell 1,325 rupiah, or about 5.9 percent, to 21,125 after ratings agency Moody's announced it could downgrade its debt.
Moody's said it had placed on review its Baa3 rating on the long-term debt of Sampoerna International Finance Co B.V.'s US$200 million notes for a possible downgrade.
It said the notes are unconditionally guaranteed by PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna.

It said the review was prompted by a series of announcements by Sampoerna on October 5 that it was convening an extraordinary general meeting. The meeting would address, among other subjects, Moody's said, the "financing and purchase of Astra shares".
A Sampoerna subsidiary has bought a 2.85 percent stake in Astra. Sampoerna president director Putera Sampoerna has bought an additional 9.81 percent in the automobile firm on his individual account.
